recommendation: Keep this empty audit commit as-is. No follow-up source edit is needed for FHIR-19501 unless CDS later wants operation comments to repeat the fuller CQL/FHIRPath examples already present in the resource notes, which would be editorial rather than necessary for current implementer understanding.
issue_request: FHIR-19501 was a Published/Persuasive CDS change request asking how CQL can access PlanDefinition and ActivityDefinition $apply parameters, and what CQL context is used for subjects that are not Patients. The accepted resolution was to document in the $apply operation that parameters are available to CQL and FHIRPath expressions evaluated during $apply as percent-prefixed environment/context variables.
initial_application: The issue was applied by 760504d5b6cf37cf71430074257a1d92922ed371, which added wording for dynamicValue parameter access to ActivityDefinition and PlanDefinition notes and to the then-spreadsheet-backed operation definitions. Current blame still attributes the explicit CQL/FHIRPath percent-variable paragraphs in the resource notes to that Jira-tagged commit, while the current OperationDefinition files retain equivalent operation-level wording after later refactors.
additional_context: FHIR-18196, resolved in the same 2018 CDS ballot cycle, changed the $apply patient parameter to subject and documented subject resolution by type. FHIR-39528 later added Clinical Reasoning guidance that subject elements establish the CQL evaluation context. FHIR-29211 later confirmed the operation-parameter context-variable pattern as a general SHOULD for operations that evaluate expressions and is already represented on the combined branch.
reconciliation: No source change was made. Current ActivityDefinition and PlanDefinition notes explicitly state that $apply parameters are available within dynamicValue CQL and FHIRPath expressions as percent-prefixed context variables, both $apply OperationDefinitions state the same operation-parameter rule, current $apply subject parameters support non-Patient subject types, and the active Clinical Reasoning Using Expressions page covers subject evaluation context and the general operation-parameter pattern.

related_jiras.note: Same ballot-cycle CDS change that renamed $apply patient to subject and resolved subject context by type, addressing the non-Patient context part of FHIR-19501.
Later Published issue asking generally for operation parameters to be available to expressions; already audited on the combined branch and supports the current no-change conclusion.
Later Applied issue clarifying that knowledge-artifact subject elements establish the CQL evaluation context.
